findings.evidence: scripts/claims_access.py:100-102 "This does NOT see people whose access comes from the organization ... `has_access` covers them."
findings.fix: Rename to what the two endpoints give, e.g. `directly_admitted` or `collaborators_and_invitees`, so the docstring's caveat becomes a note rather than a correction of the name.
findings.issue: `already_admitted` now advertises more than it returns: the new docstring states it does NOT see anyone admitted via the organization, so the name is wrong exactly for the population this PR exists to handle. A reader of `merged_pr_authors() - already_admitted()` (line 130) will believe the difference is precisely who needs admitting — the bug being fixed.

findings.evidence: scripts/claims_access.py:123 `p.stdout.strip() in ("write", "maintain", "admin")`; scripts/test_claims_access.py `test_read_only_or_no_access_still_needs_an_invitation` asserts False for `read`.
findings.fix: Rename to `can_push` (or `has_push_access`), matching the docstring "Can this login already push" and the `permission=push` grant it guards.
findings.issue: `has_access` is false for a login with `read` permission, who does have access to the repo; the function decides push capability, as its own first docstring sentence and the test name `test_read_only_or_no_access_still_needs_an_invitation` say. The name reads at the call site (line 134 `if has_access(login): continue`) as "is already a collaborator", which is a different predicate.

findings.evidence: scripts/claims_access.py:149-152 comment "204 (empty) means they could already push after all, so say what happened rather than claiming an invitation that was never sent", followed by `invited += 1`.
findings.fix: Rename to `acted` / `reported` (whatever gates the summary line), leaving `invited` for the 201 branch if a count of real invitations is wanted.
findings.issue: The counter `invited` is incremented on the 204 branch that prints `{login} already had access` (line 151-152) — the very case the PR says must not be reported as an invitation — and on the dry-run branch where nobody is invited. The name contradicts the distinction the PR introduces.

summary: The predicate names introduced or re-documented here overstate what they compute: `already_admitted` needs three lines of docstring to disclaim that it omits admitted org members, and `has_access` is true only for push-or-better. Rename both to match what they actually decide.
